System requirements speciﬁcations is a document where all system requirements of a
system to be developed are listed. The SRS document explains precisely and
expounds on functions responsibilities and capabilities of the software that it must
provide to the intended users, it must also suit the constraints that it must abide to
SRS is also used to provide the scope of the system and the tools that will
be used in development of the system. It is also used to enhance budget estimations
for the system being developed that is it gives the actual cost of the software
and hardware required in the development process.
The main objective of this document is to illustrate the requirements of the
Machine learning system. The document gives the detailed description of both
functional and non-functional requirements proposed by the client. This document is
developed after a number of consultations with farmers who do large scale and small
scale farming of potatoes and considering the complete requirement speciﬁcations of
the given project

This document is intended for prospective users of the proposed machine learning-
based potatoes disease detection system, speciﬁcally farmers. It is essential for
farmers to understand the system thoroughly, as they will be the primary users and will
regularly interact with it.

This system is designed to assist farmers by automating the detection of potato
diseases through machine learning. By simply uploading an image of a potato leaf, the
system will analyze the image to identify potential diseases, such as early or late blight,
enabling farmers to respond quickly and effectively. Recent studies indicate that
machine learning models, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), are
effective in agricultural disease detection, providing high accuracy and reliability when
applied to image classiﬁcation tasks (Kang et al., 2023; Upadhyay et al., 2024).
The system includes an intuitive interface, allowing farmers to upload images easily and
receive immediate feedback on disease presence. A machine learning model,
speciﬁcally trained for potato disease detection, ensures high accuracy in identifying
diseases, leveraging CNN architecture to achieve robust detection (Arnaud et al., 2022).
To further enhance its functionality, the system integrates OpenAI to provide farmers
with tailored recommendations and actionable advice based on the disease diagnosis.
Studies on AI-driven agricultural support show that AI integrations can offer valuable,
context-speciﬁc guidance, from treatment options to preventive measures (Paul et al.,
2019). With this integration, farmers will not only receive instant disease detection
feedback but also expert-level recommendations from OpenAI, enabling them to make
informed decisions on disease management. This combination of detection and advice
aims to empower farmers and contribute to more sustainable and productive potato
farming.
The Potato Disease Prediction System overall interface requires the user (IT literate) to u
pload an image of their potato crops. Utilizing machine learning algorithms, the system
analyzes the image and, with the help of OpenAI, predicts potential potato diseases. Inf
ormative results are produced to the user upon which a decision can be made, enabling
proactive measures to reduce crop loss and improve yield quality.

The Potato Disease Prediction System assumes that farmers have access to a smartphone or a
computer with an internet connection to upload images of potato crops. It relies on the availa
bility of quality images captured by farmers for accurate disease prediction the machine learn
ing models will be trained on a comprehensive and representative dataset to ensure high predi
tion accuracy. Farmers are expected to follow the system's guidelines for capturing images, e
nsuring clarity and relevance, and to receive adequate training to use the platform effectively.
The performance of the system depends on the availability of appropriate hardware and stable
internet connectivity for image uploads, as well as the quality and diversity of the training da
taset used for machine learning. Additionally, the system may rely on third-
party services such as cloud storage and processing platforms for data handling and model tra
ining, and on specific machine learning libraries and image processing tools. Finally, adheren
ce to data privacy laws and agricultural regulations is crucial, which may affect system deplo
yment and operation.

The system shall allow users (farmers) to upload images of potato leaves through an intuitive
interface.
Uploaded images should be stored securely in the system’s database for further analysis and
future reference.
The system shall preprocess the uploaded images to enhance quality and prepare them for
disease detection. This includes resizing, normalization, and noise reduction.
The system shall analyze uploaded images using a trained machine learning model (e.g.,
CNN) to detect and classify potato diseases, such as early blight and late blight.
The system should provide a confidence score or probability for each diagnosis to help
farmers understand the likelihood of each detected disease.
The system shall provide real-time feedback to the user with the disease identification results
once the analysis is complete.
Results should display a clear, understandable message about the detected disease or indicate
if no disease is found.
The system shall integrate OpenAI to generate tailored treatment recommendations based on
the detected disease.
Upon detection, OpenAI should provide actionable advice on treatment options, preventive
measures, and best practices for disease management.

The system shall process uploaded images and return disease detection results within 2
seconds, providing real-time feedback to users. For treatment recommendations generated
through OpenAI, the response time shall not exceed 3 seconds, ensuring an efficient user
experience. To maintain accuracy and reliability, the disease detection model is expected to
achieve a minimum accuracy rate of 90% in classifying diseases like early and late blight,
and each classification shall include a confidence score to aid users in understanding the
reliability of the results.
The system must support scalability, capable of handling up to 100 simultaneous user
requests without performance degradation, and be designed for easy scaling to accommodate
future growth. Additionally, it shall meet a minimum uptime of 99.5%, allowing reliable
access with minimal downtime for maintenance. The system is also required to process a
minimum of 100 images per minute to handle peak usage periods effectively.
Maximum Response Time
The system shall complete disease detection and classification within 3 seconds of image
upload.
OpenAI Recommendation Response Time
The system shall generate treatment recommendations through OpenAI within 5 seconds
after disease detection.
Detection Model Accuracy
The machine learning model shall achieve a minimum accuracy of 90% in detecting and
classifying diseases like early and late blight.
Simultaneous User Support
The system shall support up to 100 concurrent users without any noticeable performance
impact.
Image Processing Throughput
The system shall be capable of processing at least 100 images per minute during peak usage
periods.
System Uptime
The system shall maintain a minimum uptime of 99.5%, allowing for continuous access and
minimal interruptions.
Confidence Score Display
The system shall display a confidence score with each disease detection result, with values
ranging from 0 to 1, where 1 represents the highest confidence.
Response Time Under Load
The system’s response time shall dynamically adjust to handle increased user load, ensuring
that disease detection results are delivered within 5 to 8 seconds even with up to 100
concurrent users.
Scalability of Image Processing
The system shall scale its image processing capabilities in real time to handle up to 200
images per minute during peak usage, with a target of maintaining a 5-second response
time for detection results under normal conditions.
Adaptive Accuracy Adjustment
The system shall monitor detection accuracy dynamically, adjusting model thresholds to
maintain 90% accuracy as new data is added and the model is retrained periodically for
improved performance.
Real-Time Confidence Scoring
Confidence scores shall be updated dynamically with each detection, showing real-time
adjustments based on new or recalibrated data, with scores displayed within 1 second of
detection.

In addition to core functional requirements, there are several software attributes that, while
not direct requirements, significantly impact system performance and user experience.
Measures have been put in place to address these attributes, ensuring they are effectively
managed. By proactively considering and handling these attributes, the overall performance,
reliability, and usability of the system are greatly enhanced.
Usability
The system shall provide a user-friendly interface that is simple for farmers to navigate, even
with minimal technical expertise.
It shall use clear language and intuitive controls for uploading images and viewing results,
ensuring accessibility for all users.
Reliability
The system shall operate consistently with a target uptime of 99.5%, minimizing downtime
and ensuring availability when users need it.
It should be resilient to failures, with built-in fault tolerance to recover quickly from errors
and maintain seamless operation.
Scalability
The system shall be scalable, capable of expanding its processing power and storage as the
number of users and data volume increase.
The architecture should allow for the addition of resources or distribution of load across
multiple servers without affecting performance.
Performance
The system shall perform efficiently, providing disease detection results within a target of 5
seconds under normal load and up to 8 seconds under peak load.
The OpenAI integration shall provide treatment recommendations within 10 seconds after
disease detection to maintain a smooth user experience.
Compatibility
The system shall be compatible with multiple devices and browsers, allowing farmers to use
it on desktops, laptops, and mobile devices with standard browsers like Chrome, Safari, and
Firefox.
Maintainability
The system codebase shall be modular and well-documented, allowing developers to update,
debug, or extend the system with minimal disruption.
Regular maintenance schedules should be established to keep the system updated with the
latest improvements and security patches.
